eternal life

by exhaustedpillow

Summary

Numerous times Mydei has heard some mothers lament over their husbands' indifference towards their children, but it looks like he can rest easy from such worries.

Sitting on the sofa with their newborn daughter in his arms, Phainon looks absolutely smitten. With a dopey smile and fond expression on his face, it’s very amusing (and heartwarming) to see how the white-haired male gets all gooey over their newly born baby.

.

(though it comes with a set of behaviors he doesn't expect from his husband.)

Notes

for those who can forgive anything

loosely connected to morning light

See the end of the work for more notes

chapters.title: eternal life
chapters.html:
Mydei can’t stop the fond scoff from leaving his lips, as he not so discreetly stares at his husband. Exhaustion is still engraved deeply on his bones— a childbirth is truly nothing to scoff at, but the sight he’s currently being presented is more than enough to alleviate a good chunk of it. 

Sitting on the sofa across his bed with their newborn daughter in his arms, Phainon looks absolutely smitten. With a dopey smile and fond expression on his face, it’s very amusing (and heartwarming) to see how the white-haired male gets all gooey over their newly born baby.

(Quite a contrast too, with how hesitant and terrified Phainon was just to touch a speck of their baby’s hair at first.)

“So small and cute.” Phainon murmurs for the nth time with barely-repressed wonder, unable to resist the urge to nudge their child’s hand gently. Even his pointer finger is a comical contrast to their daughter's tinier one and it’s so apparent how adoration explodes on his face, as the white–haired male breaks out into another bright-as-the-sun smile.

Too bad that he has to put it to a stop.

“You’re going to wake her up if you keep that up.” Mydei quietly scolds, though there’s no heat in his tone. “Let her sleep, Phainon.” 

Upon hearing his admonishment, the white-haired male turns his head towards him, looking apologetic. “Sorry, but it’s just— I can’t help it.” He gushedly says. “She’s so tiny and so sooo—” 

Phainon abruptly stops talking and snaps his head back to their baby. A deep gasp is choked out of him before barely audible, uncharacteristic squeals echo from his throat as he raptly watches their child squirm and unconsciously grabs his finger with her palm.

Phainon snaps his head back to him and mouths excitedly, “Did you see that?”

“Barely a week in and I see our child has irrevocably put you under her spell.” Mydei muses as his husband’s utter excitement rubs off on him. 

“How could I not be?” Phainon whispers back, as he carefully and extremely gently pries his finger away from his daughter’s grasp. “She’s our daughter and she looks the spitting image of you.” 

“Again, she’s just a few days old, Deliverer. Surely the way she looks will change and I beg to differ— In exception of my hair color, she has most of your features rather than mine.”

“I still think she looks like you,” Phainon says with a smile. “But let’s wait and see who’s right. I bet she’ll grow up looking like you.” 

“Sure.” Mydei fondly scoffs. “But most importantly, she’s already fast asleep and it’s time for you to put her back into the crib.” He orders.

“Can’t I just hold her?” Phainon asks without lifting his gaze away from his daughter. “I can hold her until her meal time.”

“Her next meal is three hours away. You’re going to get yourself a cramp in the process.” Mydei points out reasonably. 

“No, I won’t.” Phainon denies. “Right, princess? It’s better to be held by papa, right?” He says, gently nudging his daughter’s clenched fist again.

“Yes, you will. It won’t be good in the long run either, if she gets used to being held and refuses to be put down on her bed.” Mydei sighs, reiterating what the nurses have told them after knowing that Phainon rarely lets go of their daughter once she is in his embrace.

“I don’t mind being our princess’ chair.” 

“Phainon.”

“Yes, Dei.” Phainon resignedly chuckles. With the nimbleness that he has developed recently, the white-haired prince stands up and carefully puts their sleeping baby back into her crib without jostling her once, covering her with her blanket and arranging the pillows afterward. 

“Sleep tight, princess.” Phainon quietly says, before the white-haired male turns his attention back to him. An equally tender smile is etched on his face as he approaches his bed. Sitting on the edge, Phainon gently takes his hand and rubs it softly. “How are you feeling? Would you like me to fetch you something? A snack or some cold pomegranate juice? Or would you like me to set up a warm bath followed by a fresh milk before taking a nap? ” 

“Phainon.”

“Yes, Dei? Which one do you need? Or should I get something else—”

“You’re being too fussy.” 

Phainon chuckles in disbelief. “I’m not fussy.” 

“You are.” Mydei wryly says. “I am not a fragile flower, Deliverer. So stop being overbearing.” 

“I would never dare to think of you as such.” Phainon refutes with a huff. “And this is not me being overbearing, Dei. This is me spoiling and loving you.” He corrects with a gentler tone. “You’ve done a great feat by carrying and having our child, so let me do my part too as your husband.”

“Still a smooth talker, I see.” Mydei remarks softly. A frown automatically appears on his face when he tries to move and fixes his position, completely forgetting about his not-so-ideal state and accidentally pulling on his back and thigh muscles. 

Fastidiously, Phainon sits up and easily lifts him, wordlessly knows which position he's aiming for, and helps him to ease into it without jostling him too much.

“Are you trying to win the best husband of the year, Deliverer?” Mydei remarks evenly as Phainon busies himself with tucking him back under the blanket and swiftly repositioning the pillows and bolster at the same time.

“Well, the only opinion that matters for that competition is yours, so I suppose it’ll be very biased.” Phainon responds with a chuckle, before a light frown descends on his face. “It’s been a few days, Mydei. While I don’t expect you to make a full recuperation at once, but it’s a little concerning how slow your self-recovery is compared to usual. I still remember how you fell and deeply scratched your knee, but it was all healed on the next day.” He murmurs with a worried look. “Maybe I should ask someone to retrieve that herb Krateros spoke of before and check it out with Hyacine—” 

“No, you aren’t going to do anything.” Mydei briskly orders as his right hand grasps the white-haired male’s wrist. “You’re turning into an overthinker worrywart, HKS. Don’t you ever hear the phrase that a child always takes at least half of their mother’s soul and strength?” 

“That’s not helping, Dei.” Phainon exhales deeply, not bothering to deny the accusation.

“I’m recovering from childbirth. They said it’s akin to surviving a major injury, so I expect this much knockback to my health.” Mydei points out. “More importantly, being constantly here with me is slowly driving you up with useless thoughts. Go get some air and rest away from this hospital, Phainon.” 

“I’ll be out of my mind to agree to such a thing.” The white-haired male firmly says. “I will not—”

Phainon is notably startled when he cups the other’s cheeks, pressing them together and rendering him unable to speak. 

“Listen to me and listen to me well, Phainon.” Mydei sternly says. “You are the one who needs rest and a change of scenery more than I.” 

“But—” 

“I’m not bleeding out and I won’t die at a moment’s notice— not anymore. I’m completely safe now.” 

Phainon flinches at the reminder and grits his teeth. “Mydeimos—” 

“Our daughter is all healthy too. You see it yourself.” Mydei cuts. “There’s no reason for you to run yourself ragged like this. Did you think I didn’t know how little you’ve slept on that stupidly small, guest bed?" He raises his eyebrow challengingly. “You constantly ran around to tend to me and handled some of our unavoidable duties on the day, and when night came, you were mostly the one who was awake to feed our daughter. When do you sleep— no, when was the last time you even slept for more than an hour?” 

“I’m completely fine—”

“Or did you think I won’t notice how often you stare at me, to see if I'm still breathing? Or glance at my lap to check if I was bleeding again?” Mydei ruthlessly continues. “Do you really think I’m an oblivious fool, HKS?” 

“That’s…” Phainon throws his head to the side, unable to refute anymore. “I was just worried—” 

“Look, I’m happy that you try to take your role as a husband and father properly, but I don’t want you to foolishly run yourself into a needless, nervous breakdown.” He sternly states.

“Being away from you and our daughter will only make it worse.” Phainon declares, rubbing his face with a deep sigh.

“I’m not ordering you to get out of here for a whole three days or something.” Mydei points out. “I'm asking you to leave for today, get some fresh air with an ample sleep in our bed back home, and come back here tomorrow.”

“That’s— How could I—”

Realizing that his husband genuinely won't budge without some force, Mydei crosses his hands on his chest and glares at the other. “Those are orders and not requests, Phainon. Go peacefully, or should I move and throw you out myself?” He challenges. “I might have lost half of my strength, but it’s more than sufficient to drag you out to the exit gate myself.” 

At the not-so-subtle, very real threat, Phainon churns out a tight smile. “You’re so cruel,” He wants to say, but…

“Fine.” Phainon finally relents. “But who will help you with our daughter? Surely you won’t let Krateros—” 

“Hyacine promised to come and accompany me today.” Mydei interrupts before the other can generate more excuses. “Besides, Krateros will also come with a dependable figure to help me tend to our daughter at night.”

Phainon looks confused at first, staring at him thoughtfully as if he's digging out his memories before it morphs into a deep frown, when he realizes that he has no recollection of such arrangements.

“When did—”

“When you were out doing your duties this morning.” Mydei answers promptly.

“I never heard any of these.” Phainon argues back, still wearing the deep frown.

“Hence I'm informing you now.” Mydei dryly says. "Why? You phrased it as if you should've been aware of such things.” He baits the white-haired male with a knowing look, and just as expected, Phainon instantly folds. 

“Okay.” Phainon exhales softly. “But promise me you’ll contact me as soon as there’s trouble?” 

“Phainon.” Mydei evenly says, feeling his patience thinning ever so slightly. “This hospital is built in my mother’s name and is littered with my men. Do you really think there’ll be trouble on my turf?” He raises his eyebrow challengingly. “Or is this your roundabout request to have your ass kicked out?” 

The white-haired male chuckles softly. “Alright, alright. I get your point.” He says as he leans forward to steal a kiss. 

“I’ll see you tomorrow, Dei.”

It’s five past midnight when Phainon quietly walks along the brightly lit corridor. With a form-fitting navy shirt and pants, the white-haired male looks fresh and neat despite the late hour. He nods to the nurses in charge for the night, putting down some bags of snacks on the station before resuming his walk towards his spouse’s assigned suite.

He’s about to turn when he hears a familiar chuckle. 

“My, didn’t Mydeimos tell you to rest, Phainon?” 

Startled, Phainon whirls around before a smile breaks out on his face. “Aglaea!” He calls brightly. “What are you doing here?” 

Aglaea chuckles as she stops right in front of her heir. “That should be my question, Phainon. Why are you here?” 

“Ah, well—” 

“Aglaea, the baby is fast asleep— Huh, Phai-chan?” 

“Lady Tribios?” Phainon exclaims with surprise as he turns around again. “You’re here too?” 

“Didn’t you see her from the surveillance camera you put, Phainon?” Aglaea amusedly questions with a knowing look. 

At being busted, Phainon just smiles sheepishly. “You knew?” 

“Nothing gets past my eyes.” Aglaea lightly replies before her gaze falls downward. “Quite a heavy bag you’re carrying there, Phainon.” 

“Ah, these are some food for everyone and Mydei,” Phainon says as he pulls out two drawstring bags and hands them to both women. “These are warm apple cider with ginger and some honey curds. Please have them, Aglaea, Lady Tribios.” 

“Wow Phai-chan, these look amazing.” The red-haired female remarks delightfully as she peeks into the bag.

“We will enjoy these later, thank you, Phainon.” Aglaea smiles. “But unfortunately, Mydeimos is in already asleep right now. Hyacine administered some painkillers to him around an hour ago.” She informs kindly. 

“It’s okay. He can eat these when he wakes up and feeling hungry later.” Phainon shrugs lightly. 

Tribios chuckles at his remark. “You’ve matured so much now, Phai-chan.”

“Well, I am a father now.” Phainon grins embarrassedly.

“Regardless, aren’t you supposed to be home right now, Phainon? Instead of running around buying and packing these?” Aglaea comments, shaking the bag a little. 

“Yes, you should take it easy, Phai-chan.” Tribios adds. “De said you haven’t left ever since De got admitted here.”

Phainon dismally chuckles. “How can I peacefully rest at home when my family is right here?” 

“Fair enough.” Aglaea nods. “Mydeimos did predict that you would try to cheat his order, though we certainly didn’t expect you to be here a few minutes after midnight.” She muses.

“I’d have come sooner if it weren’t you and Lady Tribios who are here with him.” Phainon shamelessly admits with a tinge of cheekiness.

Aglaea laughs lightly. “We’ll take that as compliments.” She wisely says.

“Since De is still sleeping and your child has just recently been fed, you can take it easy for a couple of hours, Phai-chan.” Tribios informs. “You should get some shut-eye too.” 

“I see.” Phainon hums. “May I ask you for a favor, Aglaea?” He turns his head towards the golden-haired woman. “If Mydei asks you, can you tell him that I arrive before dawn?”

At this, Aglaea raises her eyebrow. “Did you just ask me to lie on his face, Phainon?” 

“I’d say that it’s just distorting the truth.” Phainon charmingly says. “I do come before dawn arrives and it’s still the day after yesterday, isn’t it?”

“Phai-chan.” Tribios shakes her head.

“I think it’s still stretching it a bit too far.” Aglaea shakes her head as well. “If he ever inquires me about it, I’ll say that you arrive around his prediction.” 

“It’s more than enough. I’m sorry for the trouble.” Phainon lowers his head a little in gratitude.

The golden-haired woman exhales softly. “In any case, have you decided on a name, Phainon?” 

“Ah, we haven’t.” Phainon replies. “Mydei has yet to find a fitting name and I’ve been advised to steer clear from such things, so…” 

Aglaea chuckles. “Perhaps that’s a wise decision.”

“I know, right?” Phainon laughs. “Mydei also agrees that I have a terrible naming sense.”

“Well, it was pleasant to catch up with you Phainon, but it's time for us to go. We shouldn’t hold you back from reuniting with Mydeimos and your child any further.” Aglaea says softly. “Or would you like us to stay and help you? You really look like you need some rest.”

“You’ve done more than enough for us, Aglaea, Lady Tribios.” Phainon gently rejects with a grateful smile. “I can take it from here.” He nods determinedly.

.

It’s almost half past one in the morning when he finally slips into his husband’s suite, with him escorting both Aglaea and Tribios to the main hall first to bid them goodbye. The door is shut close behind him with barely audible click, before he quietly walks down the corridor and steps into the main room.

The tightness around his chest that's been suffocating him ever since this afternoon loosens completely, as his gaze falls towards the two most important people in his life.

Just as Aglaea informed him, both Mydei and his daughter are fast asleep in their respective bed. He gazes at them for another moment, before he makes a beeline for the bathroom; washing his hands and face before changing the shirt he’s wearing into a fresh one he keeps along with Mydei’s. After making sure that he’s all clean and safe to be near the newly born baby, he quietly emerges and makes his way to Mydei’s side first.

A sliver of sorrow washes over him when he sees that the beige-red-haired man looks uncomfortable even when he’s deep in his slumber, the aftereffect of the childbirth is still going strong in Mydei's body. Silently, he stretches his hand to retrieve a bottle of eucalyptus oil from the drawer, before gently starting to massage his husband’s tense body. There’s little he can do to the side Mydei is sleeping on as well as his chest, so he focuses on the part he can reach. From his arms, back, shoulders, and legs, he makes sure to thoroughly lather and massage everything.

Occasionally, he glances at the other's face to check if the movements have awoken the younger man, but just like the past few days, Mydei remains asleep. Hyacine informed him that his husband is prescribed a pretty strong painkiller with a small amount of a sleeping pill so he can rest properly, but it's truly unfortunate and regrettable, how these medications still can’t give Mydei a peaceful slumber.

Thankfully, the furrowed eyebrows on the Kremnoan's face gradually melt away with every massage he gives and relief fills him at the development. 

After ensuring that Mydei is properly tucked in again, Phainon goes back into the bathroom to wash his hands from the warm oil, before making his way to his daughter this time. A chuckle escapes him when he sees her scrunched up face and he lightly taps her nose as a greeting. He adjusts her pillows and her swaddling a little, before he takes a seat right beside her crib and leans on the bedrails. As he silently watches her little nose expand and shrink a little with every breath that she takes, he lets his mind wander.

Mydei was right, partially. 

He could barely get any rest these days, but it wasn’t due to their child’s feeding time, but rather the nightmare. The images are still so vivid in his mind and he can’t help but be reminded of those damning scenes whenever he closes his eyes. Of Mydei bleeding out on his hospital bed and dying, as well as the yells of panic between the healers from both sides. His hands unconsciously tremble as the stench of blood, death and the unnatural stillness from both Mydei and their newborn daughter terrorize him again.

He almost lost both of them.

Had Hyacine not arrived in time with the medications and additional blood bags, or had the healers been less adept in handling and resuscitating his daughter…

(By Kephale, he would sooner follow after them than endure such grief.)

Phainon takes a deep, sharp inhale as he wills the bad memories away, along with the slight moisture in his eyes.

While he can perfectly see that both Mydei and their daughter are fine now, the fear is still gripping his heart hard. Just like how Mydei noticed, it has become a habit of his to check on his breathing. But, Mydei has yet to know that their daughter's condition used to be just as bad as himself, and thus, he’s actually constantly checking on his and their daughter’s breathing.

It's a hard fact that he loves carrying his daughter in his arms. He's fully content and he can spend hours doing so, but in truth, it's also a convenient way to keep an eye on both Mydei and her.

Letting out another deep sigh, he lets his mind travel to a more lighthearted topic, specifically the conversation he just had with Aglaea and Tribios.

A name. 

True, their daughter's name is being waited on by everybody at this point, but they have yet to find one. With him wanting Mydei to focus on his recovery first, as well as acknowledging his poor naming skills, their child’s name has yet to be decided. 

He’s content on calling her ‘his daughter’ or ‘princess’, but truthfully, there’s a name that’s been niggling on the back of his mind.

“Athanasia.” Phainon whispers, lightly caressing her chubby cheek. “Do you think your papa will like it?” 

“I do.”

Phainon jumps out from his position, his hand halfway from pulling his hidden blade to protect his daughter before his mind registers whose voice he heard.

“Dei?” He bewilderedly exclaims before a tinge of panic of being busted sets in him.

“I’m not even going to ask why you’re already here at this hour, HKS.” Mydei wryly says as he stands right behind him, all while crossing his arms on his chest. 

“You’re supposed to be asleep, Dei.” Phainon smiles tightly.

“Too bad for you, Hyacine lessened my painkillers and voided the sleeping pill tonight.” Mydei shrugs.

“Oh.” Phainon blinks. “Did I wake you up then—?” 

“No, though it does answer my question why my body felt great when I woke up for the past days.” Mydei responds as he approaches the crib. 

“I see…” He trails off.

Wordlessly, the beige-red-haired man stretches his hand, tenderly caressing the top of their daughter's head before murmuring softly. “I was going to propose three names to you. Elena, Thalia, and Phoebe,” He muses. “But I see you’ve picked a better one.”

“I— What?”

“Athanasia.” Mydei rolls the name on his tongue. “Meaning immortality, or eternal life. A fitting name, isn’t it? Considering that she brushed so close to death.” He murmurs.

“Dei—”

“To think that you hid the fact that our daughter momentarily stopped breathing after her birth from me.” Mydei shakes his head. “How preposterous.”  

“I’m sorry.” Phainon murmurs. “I wanted you to focus on your own health first and planned to tell you later, Mydei.” 

“I admit that I was in a bad shape myself, but do it again and I won’t hesitate to pummel you to the ground next time, Phainon.” Mydei warns.

“I understand.” Phainon apologetically says. “I promise I won’t do it again.”

“Hmph, good.” Mydei replies.

Silence momentarily stretches between them, as their gazes are fixed on their sleeping daughter. 

“So, Athanasia?” Phainon inquires after a while. “Are you sure you’re okay with such meaning, Dei?” 

“The other names I picked revolve around being a ‘light’ or ‘blossoming’," Mydei explains, "But once I knew of her momentary death, I immediately changed my mind.” He quietly says. “Perhaps it’s utterly selfish of me, but I wish for her to live long and well, instead of being the ‘light’ or ‘to blossom beautifully’.”

Phainon churns out a solemn smile of his own. “It seems that we’re on the same page for that.” 

Mydei chuckles softly as he caresses her. “Athanasia, daughter of Mydeimos and Phainon, granddaughter of Gorgo.”

“May you live an eternal life, full of happiness and blessings, my child.”
